clearedSpotChecks.check: Does a validator still on tempo/v1.19.0 (evm2 66687c18) compute something different from the v1.19.1 endpoint (evm2 35aa3280) in any instruction the PoolManager uses?
clearedSpotChecks.note: Fetched Cargo.lock at tags tempo/v1.19.0 and tempo/v1.19.1: they pin evm2 66687c18 and 35aa3280, and both pin ruint 1.21.1. Fetched arithmetic.rs, bitwise.rs, i256.rs, control.rs, memory.rs, bytecode/analysis/aarch64.rs and bytecode/analysis/x86.rs at both revisions from raw.githubusercontent.com/DaniPopes/evm2 with HTTP 200, and each pair has the same sha256. The only change in host.rs is the skip_cold_load threshold moving from ColdStorageAdditionalCost to ColdStorageCost (line 75), which only decides whether the slot is loaded before an out of gas halt. The system.rs diff moves the call gas code into load_acc_and_calc_gas and a new merge_call_gas helper and adds a Host::execute_call entry point. The EIP-8037 refund on a failed call is in both revisions, so the research text calling it new in v1.19.1 is wrong, but the conclusion holds: no change to the success flag or return data of CALL, STATICCALL or DELEGATECALL.

clearedSpotChecks.check: L-879: ruint 1.21.1 as built for x86_64 against the same crate with every target_arch = "x86_64" branch forced to the non-x86 code, both against num-bigint, 30 million iterations.
clearedSpotChecks.note: The crate fetched from static.crates.io has sha256 a0de3fa9...55f2, equal to the checksum in the tempo/v1.19.1 Cargo.lock. A diff of ruint-1.21.1/src against ruint-fb/src in the work directory shows only cfg flips at algorithms/mod.rs 20, 150, 154, 160, 179, 183, 189, 206, div/reciprocal.rs 28, 31 and div/small.rs 75, 139, which are all target_arch = "x86_64" sites in the crate; the remaining target cfgs are riscv, wasm and endianness and do not apply to aarch64 little endian. out30m.txt reports 0 mismatches for both builds and 2,834,980 failures for 1.21.0, so the harness detects the known fault. The cited FullMath lines (mulmod at src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24, lt at :25, gt at :52, div at :35, :62, :67, :73) are correct. Native aarch64 code generation remains untested, as the research says.

clearedSpotChecks.check: 9,000 new vectors aimed at the ruint branches, run as creation code through eth_call on both endpoints and through eth_simulateV1 on Tempo.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I ran 400 independent random and edge vectors (MULMOD, ADDMOD, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, LT, SAR, SIGNEXTEND, EXP with 0, 1, 2^64-1, 2^128, 2^192, 2^255, 2^256-1 and neighbours) as creation code through eth_call on https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz, which reports web3_clientVersion tempo/v1.19.1-a9d6748/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu: 400 of 400 match a Python reference. On https://rpc.mainnet.arc.io, 230 of 400 were answered before the rate limit and all 230 match. This covers the x86 endpoint only, not an aarch64 validator.
